claim: Piezo1 is an ion channel that gates open when mechanical force is applied to a cell membrane.
source: Piezo1 is an ion channel that gates open when mechanical force is applied to a cell membrane, thus allowing cells to detect and respond to mechanical stimulation.
evidence: This is a well-established characterization of Piezo1 function, drawing from established scientific knowledge about this ion channel.

claim: Piezo1 allows cells to detect and respond to mechanical stimulation.
source: Piezo1 is an ion channel that gates open when mechanical force is applied to a cell membrane, thus allowing cells to detect and respond to mechanical stimulation.
evidence: This is a functional consequence of Piezo1's mechanosensitive gating, based on established knowledge.

claim: Molecular structures of Piezo1 reveal a large ion channel with an unusually curved shape.
source: Molecular structures of Piezo1 reveal a large ion channel with an unusually curved shape.
evidence: This refers to structural data from prior studies, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Piezo1 deforms the membrane shape outside the perimeter of the channel into a curved 'membrane footprint'.
source: Through membrane mechanical calculations, we show that Piezo1 deforms the membrane shape outside the perimeter of the channel into a curved 'membrane footprint'.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on membrane mechanical calculations presented in the manuscript.

claim: The membrane footprint amplifies the sensitivity of Piezo1 to changes in membrane tension.
source: This membrane footprint amplifies the sensitivity of Piezo1 to changes in membrane tension, rendering it exquisitely responsive.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion derived from the calculations and analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The shape of the Piezo channel is an example of molecular form evolved to optimize tension sensitivity.
source: We assert that the shape of the Piezo channel is an elegant example of molecular form evolved to optimize a specific function, in this case tension sensitivity.
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the functional analysis presented in the study.

claim: The predicted influence of the membrane footprint on Piezo gating is consistent with the demonstrated importance of membrane-cytoskeletal attachments to Piezo gating.
source: Furthermore, the predicted influence of the membrane footprint on Piezo gating is consistent with the demonstrated importance of membrane-cytoskeletal attachments to Piezo gating.
evidence: This connects the theoretical predictions to experimental observations from cited literature.

claim: Piezo ion channels transduce mechanical stimuli into electrical activity.
source: Piezo ion channels transduce mechanical stimuli into electrical activity (Coste et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Coste et al., 2010.

claim: Piezo1 and Piezo2 are the Piezo channels in mammals.
source: These channels – Piezo1 and Piezo2 in mammals – underlie many important processes in biology, including cell volume regulation in erythrocytes, cardiovascular system development, and touch sensation (Maksimovic et al., 2014; Ranade et al., 2014a; Ranade et al., 2014b; Cahalan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammalian Piezo channels, supported by citations.

claim: Piezo channels underlie cell volume regulation in erythrocytes, cardiovascular system development, and touch sensation.
source: These channels – Piezo1 and Piezo2 in mammals – underlie many important processes in biology, including cell volume regulation in erythrocytes, cardiovascular system development, and touch sensation (Maksimovic et al., 2014; Ranade et al., 2014a; Ranade et al., 2014b; Cahalan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: Piezo channels are exquisitely sensitive to applied mechanical force in electrophysiological experiments.
source: In electrophysiological experiments Piezo channels seem to be exquisitely sensitive to applied mechanical force: when the membrane of a cell is poked gently with a probe, or when pressure is applied to stretch a small patch of cell membrane on a gigaseal pipette, Piezo channels open (Coste et al., 2010; Lewis and Grandl, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Piezo channels open when the membrane of a cell is poked gently with a probe.
source: In electrophysiological experiments Piezo channels seem to be exquisitely sensitive to applied mechanical force: when the membrane of a cell is poked gently with a probe, or when pressure is applied to stretch a small patch of cell membrane on a gigaseal pipette, Piezo channels open (Coste et al., 2010; Lewis and Grandl, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Piezo channels open when pressure is applied to stretch a small patch of cell membrane on a gigaseal pipette.
source: In electrophysiological experiments Piezo channels seem to be exquisitely sensitive to applied mechanical force: when the membrane of a cell is poked gently with a probe, or when pressure is applied to stretch a small patch of cell membrane on a gigaseal pipette, Piezo channels open (Coste et al., 2010; Lewis and Grandl, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Purified Piezo channels reconstituted into droplet bilayers opened when force was applied by swelling a droplet.
source: In one approach Piezo channels, purified and reconstituted into droplet bilayers, opened when force was applied by swelling a droplet (Syeda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: Piezo needs only the cell membrane to couple mechanical forces to pore opening.
source: This observation implies that Piezo needs only the cell membrane to couple mechanical forces to pore opening.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the reconstitution experiment cited.

claim: Piezo channels in patches excised from cell membrane blebs open in response to pressure application.
source: In another approach, Piezo channels in patches excised from cell membrane blebs (Cox et al., 2016), or in cell excised patches with applied positive or negative pressure (Lewis and Grandl, 2015), open in response to pressure application.
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Piezo channels in cell excised patches with applied positive or negative pressure open in response to pressure application.
source: In another approach, Piezo channels in patches excised from cell membrane blebs (Cox et al., 2016), or in cell excised patches with applied positive or negative pressure (Lewis and Grandl, 2015), open in response to pressure application.
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Piezo only needs an intact lipid membrane to transduce force into pore opening.
source: These observations also support the notion that Piezo only needs an intact lipid membrane to transduce force into pore opening.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations cited.

claim: The reconstitution and excised patch experiments suggest the 'force-from-membrane' hypothesis for mechanosensitive gating.
source: The reconstitution (Syeda et al., 2016) and excised patch (Lewis and Grandl, 2015; Cox et al., 2016) experiments suggest the 'force-from-membrane' hypothesis for mechanosensitive gating, which, in its simplest form, invokes lateral membrane tension as the origin of the 'opening force' (Sukharev et al., 1999; Perozo et al., 2002; Chiang et al., 2004; Teng et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to experimental and theoretical studies.

claim: The 'force-from-membrane' hypothesis invokes lateral membrane tension as the origin of the 'opening force'.
source: The reconstitution (Syeda et al., 2016) and excised patch (Lewis and Grandl, 2015; Cox et al., 2016) experiments suggest the 'force-from-membrane' hypothesis for mechanosensitive gating, which, in its simplest form, invokes lateral membrane tension as the origin of the 'opening force' (Sukharev et al., 1999; Perozo et al., 2002; Chiang et al., 2004; Teng et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to theoretical and experimental studies.

claim: Certain properties of Piezo mechanosensitive gating change when blebs are formed on the surface of a cell by removing local cytoskeletal attachments.
source: When blebs are formed on the surface of a cell by removing local cytoskeletal attachments, certain properties of Piezo mechanosensitive gating change (Cox et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: Piezo gating is altered by applying force to a tether artificially attached to the channel.
source: And more directly, Piezo gating is altered by applying force to a tether artificially attached to the channel (Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: Membrane-mediated forces alone appear to be sufficient to open Piezo.
source: Therefore, while membrane-mediated forces alone appear to be sufficient to open Piezo, tethers attached to the membrane or to the channel itself also seem to play a role in Piezo gating.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations cited.

claim: Tethers attached to the membrane or to the channel itself also seem to play a role in Piezo gating.
source: Therefore, while membrane-mediated forces alone appear to be sufficient to open Piezo, tethers attached to the membrane or to the channel itself also seem to play a role in Piezo gating.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations cited.

claim: A partial molecular structure of a Piezo channel has been determined.
source: A partial molecular structure of a Piezo channel has been determined (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017; Saotome et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: Piezo is a trimer of 3 identical subunits that form one central pore and three long arms that extend away from the center.
source: Piezo is a trimer of 3 identical subunits that form one central pore and three long arms that extend away from the center.
evidence: This is based on structural data from cited studies.

claim: The extended arms of Piezo, which are made of transmembrane helices, do not lie in a plane.
source: A peculiar aspect of the structure is that the extended arms, which are made of transmembrane helices, do not lie in a plane as would be expected if Piezo normally resides in a planar membrane like most other ion channels.
evidence: This is based on structural data from cited studies.

claim: Piezo likely curves the cell membrane locally into a spherical dome projecting into the cell.
source: This property of the structure implied that Piezo likely curves the cell membrane locally into a spherical dome (projecting into the cell), which was confirmed by electron micrographs of small unilamellar lipid vesicles (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a structural study with electron micrographs.

claim: Electron micrographs of small unilamellar lipid vesicles confirmed that Piezo curves the cell membrane locally into a spherical dome.
source: This property of the structure implied that Piezo likely curves the cell membrane locally into a spherical dome (projecting into the cell), which was confirmed by electron micrographs of small unilamellar lipid vesicles (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to experimental data.

claim: A mechanism for membrane tension sensitivity called the membrane dome mechanism was proposed based on Piezo's demonstrated ability to curve lipid membranes locally into a dome.
source: On the basis of Piezo's demonstrated ability to curve lipid membranes locally into a dome, a mechanism for membrane tension sensitivity – called the membrane dome mechanism – was proposed (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: The dome shape provides a source of potential energy for gating in the form of excess membrane area 'stored' by curving the membrane when the membrane comes under tension.
source: Simply stated, the dome shape provides a source of potential energy for gating – in the form of excess membrane area 'stored' by curving the membrane – when the membrane comes under tension.
evidence: This is an explanation of the membrane dome mechanism based on physical principles.

claim: If the Piezo dome becomes flatter when Piezo opens, then the projected (in-plane) area of the dome will expand.
source: If the Piezo dome becomes flatter when Piezo opens, then the projected (in-plane) area of the dome will expand, that is, the available in-plane area of the membrane-Piezo system will increase.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on geometric principles.

claim: The membrane dome model only considered the shape of the membrane within Piezo's perimeter and not the shape of the surrounding membrane.
source: However, the membrane dome model of Piezo gating only considered the shape of the membrane within Piezo's perimeter and not the shape of the surrounding membrane, which is necessarily coupled to the curvature of the Piezo dome.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of the prior model.

claim: The Piezo dome can strongly curve the surrounding membrane.
source: Through membrane mechanical calculations, we show that the Piezo dome can strongly curve the surrounding membrane.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on calculations presented in the manuscript.

claim: The energetic coupling between the shape of the Piezo dome and the surrounding membrane amplifies Piezo's tension sensitivity.
source: We find that the energetic coupling between the shape of the Piezo dome and the surrounding membrane amplifies Piezo's tension sensitivity, and may explain the experimentally observed regulation of Piezo gating by membrane-cytoskeletal attachments.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion based on calculations and analysis in the manuscript.

claim: The energetic coupling between the shape of the Piezo dome and the surrounding membrane may explain the experimentally observed regulation of Piezo gating by membrane-cytoskeletal attachments.
source: We find that the energetic coupling between the shape of the Piezo dome and the surrounding membrane amplifies Piezo's tension sensitivity, and may explain the experimentally observed regulation of Piezo gating by membrane-cytoskeletal attachments.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation connecting the theoretical findings to experimental observations.

claim: The dome surface area is covered by approximately 20% protein and 80% lipid membrane.
source: The intersection of the grey surface and the Piezo channel, shown in cyan, informs that the dome surface area is covered by approximately 20% protein and 80% lipid membrane.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the structural model shown in Figure 1.

claim: If the unperturbed configuration of the lipid membrane is planar, the Piezo protein must apply a distorting force on the membrane to locally bend the membrane into a dome shape.
source: Note that, if the unperturbed configuration of the lipid membrane is planar, the Piezo protein must apply, through its curved structure, a distorting force on the membrane to locally bend the membrane into a dome shape.
evidence: This is an inference based on membrane mechanics principles.

claim: The membrane applies an opposing force on the protein.
source: And, of course, the membrane applies an opposing force on the protein.
evidence: This is based on Newton's third law and membrane mechanics principles.

claim: The result is a stable, non-planar equilibrium configuration of the membrane-Piezo system with zero net force, in which the sum energy of the channel and the membrane is minimized.
source: The result is a stable, non-planar equilibrium configuration of the membrane-Piezo system with zero net force, in which the sum energy of the channel and the membrane is minimized.
evidence: This is based on equilibrium thermodynamics principles.

claim: The curved shape of the mid-bilayer surface of the Piezo dome deforms the mid-bilayer surface of the surrounding lipid membrane.
source: The curved shape of the mid-bilayer surface of the Piezo dome (indicated in grey) deforms the mid-bilayer surface of the surrounding lipid membrane (indicated in blue) and results in a membrane footprint of Piezo that extends beyond the size of the dome (see Figure 2A for further details).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C and explained in the text.

claim: The energetic cost to curve a membrane contains a term proportional to the membrane's mean curvature squared.
source: The fundamental reason for this is, the energetic cost to curve a membrane contains a term proportional to the membrane's mean curvature squared.
evidence: This is based on the Helfrich membrane bending energy model.

claim: A sharp transition from the curved dome shape to a planar membrane is associated with a higher energy than a gradual transition.
source: As a result, a sharp transition from the curved dome shape to a planar membrane is associated with a higher energy than a gradual transition.
evidence: This is an inference based on membrane mechanics principles.

claim: The total energy of the membrane-Piezo system has to include Piezo's membrane footprint in addition to the Piezo dome.
source: The total energy of the membrane-Piezo system therefore has to include Piezo's membrane footprint in addition to the Piezo dome.
evidence: This is a logical conclusion from the analysis.

claim: Piezo's membrane footprint influences the total energy of the membrane-Piezo system.
source: As we will show, Piezo's membrane footprint not only influences the total energy of the membrane-Piezo system, but it also has a very large influence on Piezo's ability to sense changes in membrane tension.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: Piezo's membrane footprint has a very large influence on Piezo's ability to sense changes in membrane tension.
source: As we will show, Piezo's membrane footprint not only influences the total energy of the membrane-Piezo system, but it also has a very large influence on Piezo's ability to sense changes in membrane tension.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: The dominant shape of Piezo's membrane footprint corresponds to that associated with the lowest energy.
source: Of all the possible shapes Piezo's membrane footprint may adopt, we assume that the dominant shape corresponds to that associated with the lowest energy.
evidence: This is a standard assumption in equilibrium thermodynamics.

claim: Calculation of Piezo's membrane footprint and its associated energy is a well-defined mechanics problem involving no free parameters.
source: Therefore, calculation of Piezo's membrane footprint and its associated energy is a well-defined mechanics problem involving no free parameters.
evidence: This is a statement about the nature of the theoretical approach used.

claim: If Piezo becomes flatter when it opens, then the deformation footprint will contribute to the energetics of gating.
source: If Piezo becomes flatter when it opens, as was proposed in the membrane dome mechanism (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017), then the deformation footprint will contribute to the energetics of gating, as shown (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B and explained in the text, with reference to a prior hypothesis.

claim: Piezo's membrane footprint would impose a tension-dependent bias, favoring the open conformation of Piezo only when tension is applied, and more so when tension is greater.
source: Thus, Piezo's membrane footprint would impose a tension-dependent bias, favoring the open conformation of Piezo only when tension is applied, and more so when tension is greater.
evidence: This is an inference based on the energy calculations.

claim: The special surface where principal curvatures sum to zero is called a catenoid.
source: This special surface, called a catenoid, would never truly be achieved in this physical system because thermal fluctuations will not permit zero tension and, potentially, because of deviations of the Piezo dome from a perfect spherical cap.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of minimal surfaces in differential geometry.

claim: A catenoid would never truly be achieved in this physical system because thermal fluctuations will not permit zero tension.
source: This special surface, called a catenoid, would never truly be achieved in this physical system because thermal fluctuations will not permit zero tension and, potentially, because of deviations of the Piezo dome from a perfect spherical cap.
evidence: This is an inference based on physical considerations.

claim: In the absence of applied tension the deformation footprint should approach the approximate shape of a catenoid.
source: Nevertheless, in the absence of applied tension the deformation footprint should approach the approximate shape of a catenoid.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mathematical analysis.

claim: For tension values likely relevant to Piezo gating, the contribution to the Piezo gating energy due to Piezo's membrane footprint is approximately equal to or greater than the tension-dependent contribution due to the Piezo dome itself.
source: In all three cases, for tension values likely relevant to Piezo gating, the contribution to the Piezo gating energy due to Piezo's membrane footprint is approximately equal to or greater than the tension-dependent contribution due to the Piezo dome itself.
evidence: This is shown in Figures 4A-C and explained in the text.

claim: Using the analytical approach for calculating Piezo's membrane footprint, the tension sensitivity grows without bound as the membrane tension approaches zero.
source: In fact, using the analytical approach for calculating Piezo's membrane footprint it can be shown that the tension sensitivity grows without bound as the membrane tension approaches zero.
evidence: This is based on the analytical solution presented in the appendix.

claim: Piezo's membrane footprint renders Piezo exquisitely sensitive in the low-tension regime; most sensitive to the smallest perturbations around zero tension.
source: This remarkable result means that Piezo's membrane footprint renders Piezo exquisitely sensitive in the low-tension regime; most sensitive to the smallest perturbations around zero tension.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the analytical result.

claim: Membrane bending stiffness is a function of lipid composition.
source: We are interested in this dependence because membrane bending stiffness is a function of lipid composition, which could vary among different cell types and possibly even between different regions within the same cell.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of membrane biophysics.

claim: Membrane bending stiffness could vary among different cell types and possibly even between different regions within the same cell.
source: We are interested in this dependence because membrane bending stiffness is a function of lipid composition, which could vary among different cell types and possibly even between different regions within the same cell.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of membrane biophysics.

claim: Piezo channels in different cell types and possibly different locations within a cell will exhibit different gating characteristics.
source: This implies that Piezo channels in different cell types and possibly different locations within a cell will exhibit different gating characteristics.
evidence: This is an inference based on the dependence of gating on membrane bending stiffness.

claim: The membrane footprint induced by Piezo is expected to influence the distribution of molecules – both lipids and proteins – in the surrounding membrane.
source: The membrane footprint induced by Piezo is expected to influence the distribution of molecules – both lipids and proteins – in the surrounding membrane.
evidence: This is an inference based on membrane-mediated interactions.

claim: Piezo's membrane footprint should attract lipids and proteins that exhibit an energetic preference for the curved shape of the membrane footprint.
source: Piezo's membrane footprint should attract lipids and proteins that exhibit an energetic preference for the curved shape of the membrane footprint, and repel molecules that 'prefer' other membrane shapes.
evidence: This is an inference based on membrane-mediated interactions.

claim: Piezo's membrane footprint should repel molecules that 'prefer' other membrane shapes.
source: Piezo's membrane footprint should attract lipids and proteins that exhibit an energetic preference for the curved shape of the membrane footprint, and repel molecules that 'prefer' other membrane shapes.
evidence: This is an inference based on membrane-mediated interactions.

claim: The composition of the surrounding membrane should influence the energetics of Piezo gating.
source: Conversely, our model of Piezo's membrane footprint implies that the composition of the surrounding membrane should influence the energetics of Piezo gating.
evidence: This is an inference based on the model.

claim: Piezo channels should interact with each other through the membrane.
source: The membrane footprint induced by Piezo also implies that Piezo channels should interact with each other through the membrane, and hence influence each other's local distribution in the membrane and gating properties.
evidence: This is an inference based on membrane-mediated interactions.

claim: Piezo channels should influence each other's local distribution in the membrane and gating properties.
source: The membrane footprint induced by Piezo also implies that Piezo channels should interact with each other through the membrane, and hence influence each other's local distribution in the membrane and gating properties.
evidence: This is an inference based on membrane-mediated interactions.

claim: Cytoskeletal attachments occur at spatial frequencies of up to tens of nanometers.
source: For example, cytoskeletal attachments, which occur at spatial frequencies of up to tens of nanometers, can restrict the shapes a membrane can take (Kusumi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: Cytoskeletal attachments can restrict the shapes a membrane can take.
source: For example, cytoskeletal attachments, which occur at spatial frequencies of up to tens of nanometers, can restrict the shapes a membrane can take (Kusumi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: The effects of membrane compartmentalization are greater in the low-tension regime.
source: In general, the effects of membrane compartmentalization are greater in the low-tension regime.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B and explained in the text.

claim: The smaller the membrane compartment, the greater influence it has on Piezo gating.
source: We also note that the smaller the membrane compartment, the greater influence it has on Piezo gating.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B and explained in the text.

claim: Membrane compartmentalization can have a large effect on Piezo gating because membrane compartments can alter the shape and therefore the energy of Piezo's membrane footprint.
source: The important point is that membrane compartmentalization can have a large effect on Piezo gating because membrane compartments can alter the shape and therefore the energy of Piezo's membrane footprint.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the calculations shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Experimentally observed effects of cytoskeletal removal on some properties of Piezo gating could reflect the importance of Piezo's membrane footprint for Piezo gating.
source: Experimentally observed effects of cytoskeletal removal on some properties of Piezo gating could reflect the importance of Piezo's membrane footprint for Piezo gating (Cox et al., 2016).
evidence: This connects the theoretical predictions to experimental observations with citation.

claim: Contributions to the membrane bending energy due to the Gaussian membrane curvature may further modulate Piezo gating in compartmentalized membranes with heterogeneous lipid compositions.
source: Contributions to the membrane bending energy due to the Gaussian membrane curvature may therefore further modulate Piezo gating in compartmentalized membranes with heterogeneous lipid compositions.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about additional effects not included in the main analysis.

claim: Piezo channels can exhibit complex gating properties, including inactivation and voltage dependence.
source: While Piezo channels can exhibit complex gating properties, including inactivation and voltage dependence, their dominant functional characteristic is that they open in response to mechanical force (Coste et al., 2010; Lewis and Grandl, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The dominant functional characteristic of Piezo channels is that they open in response to mechanical force.
source: While Piezo channels can exhibit complex gating properties, including inactivation and voltage dependence, their dominant functional characteristic is that they open in response to mechanical force (Coste et al., 2010; Lewis and Grandl, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Piezo, owing to its unusual shape, imposes a large structural perturbation – a deformation called a membrane footprint – on its surrounding membrane.
source: And the inescapable conclusion is that Piezo, owing to its unusual shape, imposes a large structural perturbation – a deformation called a membrane footprint – on its surrounding membrane.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: Piezo's membrane footprint can come with a large energetic cost depending on the applied membrane tension.
source: Depending on the applied membrane tension, Piezo's membrane footprint can come with a large energetic cost.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: If Piezo changes its shape, for example if it becomes flatter upon opening, then the surrounding membrane will weigh in prominently in an energetic sense to Piezo's tension sensitivity.
source: Consequently, if Piezo changes its shape, for example if it becomes flatter upon opening, then the surrounding membrane will weigh in prominently in an energetic sense to Piezo's tension sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the energy calculations.

claim: Piezo's membrane footprint weighs in in such a way that the tension sensitivity of Piezo gating is greatest in the low-tension regime.
source: Moreover, Piezo's membrane footprint weighs in in such a way that the tension sensitivity of Piezo gating is greatest in the low-tension regime.
evidence: This is shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: This property would seem to render Piezo poised to respond to the slightest changes in cell membrane tension.
source: This property would seem to render Piezo poised to respond to the slightest changes in cell membrane tension.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the high sensitivity at low tension.

claim: Deviations from a spherical dome shape will alter the shape and energetics of the membrane footprint.
source: In our analysis of Piezo's membrane footprint we used a spherical dome shape to approximate a more complex underlying geometry of Piezo. Deviations from a spherical dome shape will alter the shape and energetics of the membrane footprint.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the limitations of the model.

claim: The basic idea that Piezo's curved shape will create an energetically important membrane footprint will still apply despite deviations from a spherical dome shape.
source: But the basic idea that Piezo's curved shape will create an energetically important membrane footprint will still apply.
evidence: This is a statement about the robustness of the main conclusion.

claim: Piezo's large membrane footprint rationalizes what at first seemed to be a contradiction in the experimental literature.
source: Piezo's large membrane footprint rationalizes what at first seemed to be a contradiction in the experimental literature.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the theoretical findings to experimental observations.

claim: A large membrane footprint essentially demands that both membrane-mediated forces and tether attachments be energetically important.
source: A large membrane footprint essentially demands that both contributions be energetically important.
evidence: This is an inference based on the size of the membrane footprint.

claim: Piezo's shape evolved specifically to exploit the physical properties of the lipid membrane to create a large membrane footprint, enabling exquisite tension sensitivity.
source: We think that this shape evolved specifically to exploit the physical properties of the lipid membrane to create a large membrane footprint, enabling exquisite tension sensitivity.
evidence: This is a speculative evolutionary interpretation of the findings.

claim: The Monge parametrization of surfaces tends to overestimate the magnitudes of Piezo's membrane footprint and its associated membrane deformation energy.
source: We find that the Monge parametrization of surfaces tends to overestimate the magnitudes of Piezo's membrane footprint and its associated membrane deformation energy but yields, for the scenarios considered in the main text figures, qualitatively similar predictions as the arclength parameterization of surfaces.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the two methods in Appendix 1.

claim: The Monge parametrization yields qualitatively similar predictions as the arclength parameterization of surfaces for the scenarios considered in the main text figures.
source: We find that the Monge parametrization of surfaces tends to overestimate the magnitudes of Piezo's membrane footprint and its associated membrane deformation energy but yields, for the scenarios considered in the main text figures, qualitatively similar predictions as the arclength parameterization of surfaces.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the two methods in Appendix 1.
